'''Kurt Kremer''' (born 17 June 1956 in Kapellensüng ([[Lindlar]])) is a German [[physicist]].

== Career ==
Kremer studied physics from 1974 to 1980 at the [[University of Cologne]], where he also did his PhD in 1983 under supervision of [[Kurt Binder]].<ref name=aps /> From 1982 to 1984 he was part of the scientific staff at [[Forschungszentrum Jülich]]. Following this work he worked as a postdoc at Exxon Research and Engineering Co., [[Annandale, New Jersey]] and returned to  [[Forschungszentrum Jülich|Jülich]] after his Habilitation at the [[University of Mainz]] in 1988.<ref name=aps /> After several research visits (e.g. at the [[University of Minnesota system|University of Minnesota]], Minneapolis and [[UC Santa Barbara]]) he left the research center when he became director and scientific member of the [[Max Planck Institute for Polymer Research]] in [[Mainz]] in 1995 (1998–2000 and 2008–2010 he was managing director).

His main research targets are [[theoretical physics]] and [[physical chemistry]] of especially biological and synthetic macromolecular materials, the development and application of (multiscale) computer simulation methods, as well as structure process property relations, morphology and dynamics of [[polymer]]s, [[polyelectrolytes]], gels, membranes, liquid crystals and peptides in bulk and under geometrical constraints and polymers for electronic applications. As of June 2015 he authored more than 260 scientific publications ([[ResearcherID]]: G-5652-2011). His most-cited paper ''Dynamics of entangled linear polymer melts:  A molecular‐dynamics simulation'',<ref name="Kremer Grest pp. 5057–5086">{{cite journal | last1=Kremer | first1=Kurt | last2=Grest | first2=Gary S. | title=Dynamics of entangled linear polymer melts: A molecular-dynamics simulation | journal=The Journal of Chemical Physics | publisher=AIP Publishing | volume=92 | issue=8 | date=15 April 1990 | issn=0021-9606 | doi=10.1063/1.458541 | pages=5057–5086| bibcode=1990JChPh..92.5057K }}</ref> co-authored with [[Gary S. Grest]], introduces a polymer model later to be knows as the Kremer-Grest Model.

Kremer is an elected member of the German National [[Academy of Sciences Leopoldina]] (2012),<ref name="Nationale Akademie der Wissenschaften Leopoldina 2021">{{cite web | title=Mitglieder | website=Nationale Akademie der Wissenschaften Leopoldina | date=25 September 2021 | url=https://www.leopoldina.org/mitgliederverzeichnis/mitglieder/member/Member/show/kurt-kremer/ | language=de | access-date=12 January 2022}}</ref> a fellow of the [[American Physical Society]] (2006)<ref name=aps>{{cite web|title=2011 Polymer Physics Prize Recipient|url=http://www.aps.org/programs/honors/prizes/prizerecipient.cfm?last_nm=Kremer&first_nm=Kurt&year=2011|website=APS physics|publisher=American physical society|accessdate=4 August 2015}}</ref> and Distinguished Professor of Materials Science and Chemical Engineering, University of Minnesota (1991).<ref name=aps /> He received the [[Walter Schottky Prize]] of the German Physical Society (1992),<ref name=aps /> the American Physical Society Polymer Physics Prize (2011) and an ERC-Advanced Grant (2014).
